problem: End-to-end DRL for RGBD PointNav in Habitat regresses actions directly from pixels, which is data-inefficient and takes days of GPU training; long start-goal paths make exploration hard.
motivation: Decoupling perception from control and easing the task with a curriculum could speed up training and improve the final policy. A traditional planner (A*) can supply intermediate goals during training only, so no planner is needed at deployment.
key_idea: Pre-train a twin RGB/depth VAE for perception, then train a PPO PointNav policy with an A*-guided curriculum that gradually moves the sub-goal from near the start to the true target.
insight: Intermediate A* waypoints make navigation far easier: WP-N agents reach SR >0.98 and SPL >0.85 versus 0.852/0.73 for plain PointNav. The curriculum bootstraps the final PointNav policy, and SWP-10 reaches SPL 0.91 vs 0.73 (single scene). Sampled latent z with Nz=128 trains better than mu_z or Nz=256, which the authors attribute to regularization and exploration noise and over-fitting (training-curve figure only).
method: Twin VAE: separate RGB and depth VAEs (10 conv layers, 4x4 filters, 64-512 maps, 192x192 input, latent Nz=128) pre-trained on images collected at 10° increments over 360° sweeps at random locations; only the encoders are used for the policy.

State: concatenation of z_RGB, z_depth, the pointgoal reading and the heading angle, fed to PPO. The policy is FC 512-256 (tanh), then an LSTM of 256, then policy and value heads. Actions are forward 0.25 m and turn ±10°; Done is executed automatically within 0.2 m of the goal.
A* guidance: A* on the bird's-eye-view map gives a path from start to target, and sub-goals are placed along it in training only.
WP-N: the A* path is split into N equidistant waypoints, and the goal switches on reaching within 0.2 m. This needs A* at test time, so it is used only to demonstrate the idea.
SWP-N curriculum: N is decreased in stages (10, 8, 6, 4, 3, 2, 1) over episodes, ending as plain PointNav.
FWP curriculum: a single waypoint moves linearly from 20% to 100% of the A* path over 64k episodes, ending as plain PointNav.
Reward and training: the Habitat reward (S=10, lambda=-0.01, distance-shaping), PPO with gamma 0.95, clip 0.1, GAE 1.0, Adam.

setting.backbone: Twin VAE encoders (pre-trained) + PPO policy (FC + LSTM), trained from scratch
setting.training_data: VAE trained on RGB/depth images from the Gibson Quantico scene (batch 64, 50k iterations); PPO trained in simulation on Quantico for ~100k+ episodes; transfer to the Pleasant scene by fine-tuning for ~60k episodes
setting.observation: RGBD (256x256 resized to 192x192) + pointgoal sensor + heading sensor
setting.action_space: low-level: FORWARD 0.25 m / TURN LEFT 10° / TURN RIGHT 10° (Done executed automatically within 0.2 m of goal)
setting.simulator: Habitat (Gibson Quantico scene; Pleasant for transfer)
setting.privileged: A* on the BEV map for sub-goals during training only (WP-N also needs it at test time); pointgoal/GPS-like sensor at test time

numbers.eval_set_note: 500 random test episodes in the single Quantico scene

numbers_note: The baseline PointNav is SPL 0.73 / SR 0.852 (not the paper's own method). Evaluation is on a single Gibson scene, not the standard Habitat benchmark split, so the 'val' split label is approximate. WP-N agents (SPL 0.85-0.92, SR 0.983-0.998) need A* at test time and are omitted.
results: On the Quantico scene, SWP-10 reaches SPL 0.91 and SR 0.96 and FWP reaches SPL 0.77 and SR 0.9, versus 0.73/0.852 for the plain PointNav baseline, and both train faster in episodes. Transfer to the Pleasant scene gives SPL 0.87 and SR 0.95 after ~60k episodes.
limitations: Evaluated on a single Gibson scene (plus one transfer scene), with no comparison to published Habitat baselines or the standard benchmark.
Requires a BEV map and A* during training, and the pointgoal sensor at test time; the curriculum schedule is hand-designed.
Transfer learning is only briefly examined, and the SWP curriculum shows performance drops during the later stages.
